reason: The text explicitly names four characters: Samuel (שְׁמוּאֵל), Eli (עֵלִי), Hophni (חָפְנִי), and Phinehas (פִּֽינְחָֽס). All four hold positions of authority: Eli is a priest and judge; Hophni and Phinehas are priests associated with the ark of the covenant; Samuel becomes a prophet and is ultimately recognized as a trusted messenger of God. The wife of Phinehas is mentioned but not given a personal name—she is identified only by relationship ('wife of Phinehas'). All other individuals in the passage (the messenger, the elders, servants, soldiers) are referred to only by role or collective designation, not by personal names.
